_comment: EXAMPLE recruiting filter. Replace every value with your own search.
The single source of truth for what you are recruiting for: read by the
worker (Gmail alerts, 12Twenty, job boards, people to reach out to) and by
the page, so the filters that rank a role and the copy that describes your
search cannot drift apart. Change it here and everything downstream follows.
functions are in priority order: the first is worth the most points.
headline: MBA Candidate at Harvard Business School | Seeking Summer 2027 Internship in Product & Strategy

exclude._comment: Words in a title that mean 'not for me', whatever else matches.
exclude._seniority_comment: Roles an MBA intern cannot take.
exclude._employers_comment: Employers, not words in a title — e.g. a whole industry you are not recruiting in. Matched against a company name with a word boundary in front and a negative lookahead behind, so "strategy\\s*&" style patterns work and "ey" would not match "Eyewear". Regex syntax is allowed.
exclude._sectors_comment: Sectors you are not recruiting into, matched against employer and title together as words. A function match in the wrong sector is still the wrong role.

_companies_comment: Companies you are targeting. Gmail news and recruiting mail that names one ranks higher.
_job_boards_comment: Public job boards the worker reads twice a day (worker/jobs.mjs). kind is greenhouse or ashby; slug is the name in the board URL, e.g. boards.greenhouse.io/<slug> or jobs.ashbyhq.com/<slug>. These are examples of the format.
